attempts.summary: On node1, built an LVM logical volume (data_vg/data_lv) mounted at /srv/data using two loop-backed PVs (root disk had no spare partition), initially sized ~956M, then grew it live to 2.49G via vgextend+lvextend+xfs_growfs while it stayed mounted and its test file remained intact. Set up a systemd oneshot unit (data-lv-loop-setup.service) plus an fstab entry with x-systemd.requires so the loop devices, VG activation, and mount are fully reconstructed at boot. Restarted node1 twice via `systemctl reboot`: the first reboot exposed a systemd ordering cycle (fixed by removing local-fs.target Requires/dependency loop and switching to DefaultDependencies=no/Before=local-fs.target), and the second reboot verified the fix — boot ID changed, and /srv/data came back mounted at 2.5G with matching data checksum and no failed units, with no manual intervention.
